A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be a [[Definition:Matrix|matrix]] over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].
Then the [[Definition:Row Rank|row rank]] of $\mathbf A$ equals its [[Definition:Column Rank|column rank]].

B_source.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be a [[Definition:Matrix|matrix]].
Then the [[Definition:Column Rank|column rank]] of $\mathbf A^\intercal$ is the dimension of the span of the columns of $\mathbf A^\intercal$, which are the rows of $\mathbf A$.

object_map.reformulation: Transpose the matrix, which turns rows into columns, so 'row rank' becomes 'column rank of the transpose'.

validity_conditions: Row rank of A is by definition the column rank of A^T (rows of A are columns of A^T).
The nontrivial content - that colrank(A) = colrank(A^T) - is what the proof must establish (e.g. via A = CR factorization or dimension of the image of A and A^T).
Transposition is an involution, giving the row/column symmetry.
proof_plan: By definition, the row rank of $\mathbf A$ is the column rank of $\mathbf A^\intercal$.

The column rank of $\mathbf A$ equals the largest $r$ such that $\mathbf A$ has an invertible $r \times r$ [[Definition:Submatrix|submatrix]].
As $\map \det {\mathbf B^\intercal} = \map \det {\mathbf B}$, this characterization is symmetric in rows and columns, so $\operatorname {colrank} \mathbf A = \operatorname {colrank} \mathbf A^\intercal$.
